correctness.rationale: The claim is rigorously reduced by convex automorphism averaging to three edge weights; a complete eigenvalue decomposition yields the hub contrast, class contrast, and all cycle Fourier eigenvalues. The extremal Fourier minimax has a unique feasible optimum; the remaining one-variable minimax gives closed forms for a and b and the exact admissible interval for c. The integer threshold follows from exact parity-sensitive trigonometric bounds. The supplementary checker independently agrees with 209 phase cases, 98 linear programs, and 50 direct spectra; these finite checks are not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2004 general convex FMMC method and the 2009 exact single-hub wheel result are prior art. Full relevant wheel-section material was inspected, and the present r>=2 clique-cycle join is distinguished by a new hub-contrast mode, exact full interval of invariant optimizers, and an integer hub-saturation threshold absent from the single-hub statement. Targeted alternative graph-name searches and mathematical-record comparisons found no dominating same-domain claim; incomplete indexing remains a genuine risk.

value.rationale: Clique-cycle joins are a natural multiple-hub generalization of the classical wheel, motivated by symmetric constrained Markov mixing. The exact all-parameter rate, edge probability formulas, complete invariant optimizer interval and sharp n=2r+1 versus n=2r+2 spoke-saturation boundary resolve a nontrivial network-design question that differs from the known saturated single-hub solution. The boundary and extra hub-contrast mode have clear structural content beyond a routine substitution.
